messages.subject: RE: Varying Transect Lengths in oSCR
parts:
Hi Katherine,

 

Secr just does what Andy suggests, so no software option is more appropriate in that sense. Here how I approached this in a scat transect paper a few years back.

 

1.      I created a mesh of pixels that includes all pixels *ever sampled*, and let’s say for arguments sake, the pixels are 50m x 50m. I call these all ‘traps’ every ‘deployed’.

2.      Then, defining my occasions appropriately (e.g., if one cycle of transects took 1 week, then occasion 1 is the first week), I use a function to simply ask whether the pixel was visited in an occasion (transect intersects pixel=1, 0 otherwise). This produces the trap operation object. Note that it doesn’t matter whether transects were similar lengths in each occasion as you can generate trap-by-occasion covariate determining which visit it is for the specific pixel (Indeed, in Sutherland et al 2018 Scientific Reports, we did exactly this because transects changed between visits and we needed to track which pixels had been sampled, and hence were considered ‘cleared’)

3.      Then, because each pixel now has a unique ID you can construct encounter histories by querying which pixel a scat was found in and when (i.e., which occasion),

 

I have a ‘development’ function called tracks2traps that I have shared with folks who it seems to have worked well for. I’m in the middle of moving house so it will take me a couple of days to find the most recent version, but perhaps someone on here has the function and they can share? I also have a Masters student who developed an nice general workflow for doing exactly what you describe – I can put you in touch if you like?

 

Hope that helps?

 

Chris

Dr. Royle, 

 

That method could solve my problem; however, our transects did not have a standardized starting point or path. This method was used to target areas where elk were recently seen in the fields and to sample a variety of places within the larger fields. The serpentine and random nature the technicians took through the fields would make it nearly impossible to break the hundreds of transects apart in a standardized way that makes sense. I recently learned about the transect/polygon tool in the package secr. Would this package be a better fit for my study design?

 

Katherine 

On Monday, June 1, 2020 at 3:18:53 PM UTC-4, Jeffrey Royle wrote:

ok I think I get it now.  I would recommend chopping each transect up into small bits (100 or 200m) and then each of those segments should be a trap (or detector). Thus you might have several hundred such detectors. 

Then the TDF should have only values of 1 (sampled) or 0 (not) during each of the samples occasions.

regards

andy

 

 

On Mon, Jun 1, 2020 at 3:12 PM Katherine Kurth <kathy...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Dr. Royle, 

 

Thank you for the book chapter and your response! While a distance model could work for my study, I would like to use a scr model as the elk are not equally distributed across the landscape and the agency is very interested in the spatial component. I have the spatial data for the transects, scat collected, and the collection fields themselves to use a scr model. I also have scat collected from the same elk at different detection locations and days. I am hoping someone has an idea/example of how to use transect distance to represent search effort within oSCR if what I already tried is not allowed within the package. Thank you for your time!

 

Katherine

 

On Monday, June 1, 2020 at 12:47:33 PM UTC-4, Jeffrey Royle wrote:

hi Katherine,

 

 I don't think this problem is a spatial capture-recapture problem but perhaps instead a distance sampling problem.  

 Please check out chapter 8 from AHM1 (attached) and see if that type of model is better suited.

regards

andy

 

 

On Mon, Jun 1, 2020 at 11:15 AM Katherine Kurth <kathy...@gmail.com> wrote:

I conducted elk scat surveys with transect distances varying by sampling field and day. My tdf is organized with each field as a 'trap' and then the trapping date. My code runs when the cells are binary; however, when I put the distance sampled (km) for each sampling occasion/field my model won't run and says "Error in nlm(msLL.sex, scrFrame = scrFrame, p = pv, pn = pn, D = D, nG = nG,  : non-finite value supplied by 'nlm'." Is the tdf constrained to binary or is there something else wrong with my distances? Attached is my sample tdf. I would appreciate any advice, thank you!
